target: जहाँ हम पिछली बार रुके थे, वहीं इस बार भी रुकेंगे।
english: We'll stay in the same place we stayed last time.
reason: Straight proverb ("where there's a will, there's a way") — a motto, not something a learner needs to produce. Replacement keeps the same जहाँ…वहीं correlative in an ordinary travel plan.

target: जो सबसे पहले पहुँचेगा, वो सीट पकड़ लेगा।
english: Whoever gets there first will grab the seats.
reason: Textbook motto ("one who studies will progress") — preachy and says nothing usable. Replacement keeps the जो…वो correlative with future tense in a real situation.

target: यह वही किताब है जो मैंने तुम्हें दी थी।
english: This is the same book I gave you.
reason: Proverb-style aphorism about knowledge as wealth — moralising, never spoken. Replacement keeps the वही…जो relative-correlative in everyday speech.

target: यह वो दुकान है जिसका मालिक मेरा दोस्त है।
english: This is the shop whose owner is my friend.
reason: Preachy metaphor ("family is like a tree") — reads like a poster slogan. Replacement keeps the जिसका relative clause in a normal conversational sentence.

target: जो कुछ भी हो, मुझे फ़ोन ज़रूर करना।
english: Whatever happens, be sure to call me.
reason: Moralising ("don't give up honesty"). Replacement keeps the identical जो कुछ भी हो opener plus a polite imperative that people actually say.

target: इस स्कूल में हिंदी भी पढ़ाई जाती है।
english: Hindi is also taught at this school.
reason: Niche institutional content (religious education at a monastery) a learner will never use. Replacement keeps the same locative + habitual passive (दी/पढ़ाई जाती है) with an everyday subject.

target: बच्चों के शोर से मेरा सिर दुखने लगा।
english: The children's noise gave me a headache.
reason: Literary/decorative ("the house echoed with gleeful shrieks") — written-Hindi flourish, not speech. Replacement keeps the same X से + resulting-state structure in plain spoken register.

target: मौसम ठीक हो तो हम छत पर बैठते हैं।
english: If the weather is fine, we sit up on the roof.
reason: Proverb ("if the foundation is strong, the building stands") — a motto. Replacement keeps the same … हो तो … conditional pattern in an ordinary habit.

target: भैया बाज़ार से सब्ज़ी लेकर आए।
english: My brother brought vegetables from the market.
reason: Bullock-cart village trivia — decorative and useless for a modern learner. Replacement keeps the same X से Y लेकर आया pattern with everyday vocabulary.

target: मुझे समझ नहीं आया, इसलिए मैंने टीचर से सवाल पूछा।
english: I didn't understand, so I asked the teacher a question.
reason: Stilted textbook sentence; जिज्ञासु is literary and no one describes a student that way. Replacement keeps सवाल पूछा and adds the node's इसलिए connective in natural speech.

target: मुझे यह रिपोर्ट कल शाम तक पूरी करनी होगी।
english: I have to finish this report by tomorrow evening.
reason: "आज तक" reads as "until now / so far", not "by today" — the sentence is unnatural and contradicts its English. Replacement keeps the same तक deadline + करनी होगी obligation, said the way people say it.

target: किरण हमेशा अपना फ़ोन घर पर भूल जाता है।
english: Kiran always forgets his phone at home.
reason: Near-duplicate of hi-2490 ("uses new technology") with only the name and verb swapped, and the content is vacuous. Replacement keeps हमेशा + habitual present with a concrete everyday situation.

target: सुबह उठकर चाय पीना मुझे बहुत अच्छा लगता है।
english: I really enjoy having tea after I get up in the morning.
reason: Good-habits textbook motto ("brushing your teeth is a good habit") — preachy. Replacement keeps the same उठकर + infinitive-as-subject structure in a personal, natural sentence.

target: नानी शाम को बैठकर स्वेटर बुनती थीं।
english: Grandma used to sit and knit a sweater in the evening.
reason: मचिया is a regional/dialect word a learner will never meet, and the verb-final inversion is poetic word order. Replacement keeps the बैठकर + habitual past with standard vocabulary and normal word order.

target: गर्मियों में हम नानी के घर जाते थे।
english: In summers we used to go to grandma's house.
reason: Rural trivia (drinking milk straight after milking a buffalo) — no everyday use. Replacement keeps the same season + habitual past frame with vocabulary a learner needs.

english: Dad used to read the newspaper early in the morning.
reason: Household-servant scene is dated, class-loaded and useless as a model sentence. Replacement keeps सुबह-सुबह + habitual past with a subject and action a learner will actually reuse.

target: पहले घर-घर में लैंडलाइन फ़ोन होता था।
english: Earlier every house had a landline phone.
reason: Niche cultural trivia (the tulsi platform) that teaches vocabulary nobody needs. Replacement keeps the identical पहले घर-घर में … होता था frame with an everyday object.

target: बच्चों को लकड़ी का खिलौना बहुत पसंद आया।
english: The children really liked the wooden toy.
reason: काठ is archaic/literary; the normal word is लकड़ी. Replacement keeps the same का genitive + पसंद आया construction with the word people actually use, and a natural word order.
